title: Station verdict v1 - the signable body
description: DEPART, as one file: this station verified this candidate against ITS OWN contract and states whether the candidate may leave. It is the accumulating signature of the line - a station's DEPART is the next station's ADMIT input, which is why the chain has no gaps by construction. THIS IS THE BODY, NOT THE ENVELOPE. cosign signs this file's bytes; the in-toto statement that wraps it is `station-verdict-attestation.schema.json` and building it is lane B's job, deliberately out of scope here so the body can be rendered, diffed and reviewed by a human who is not holding a key. Note the one difference from the attestation: the attestation can only ever carry ELIGIBLE, because a failed verification simply produces no signature - this body can carry REFUSED, because a refusal is a fact a station records for the record even when nothing signs it.

station.description: The cell that rendered this (e.g. `station-3-staging`). The downstream ADMIT matches this against the station its contract requires a verdict from; a verdict from the wrong station is refused rather than counted.

manifest_sha256.description: The consist manifest that defined what `what` means. Carried so a downstream station can check that the verdict it inherits and the cargo it received describe the same candidate - the identity check that the 2026-08-31 stale-bot failure had no way to perform.

contract_sha256.description: The bytes of the law this verdict was rendered under. An amended contract produces a different hash, so a verdict never silently survives the rule it was issued against.

values_proven_sha256.description: sha256 of the compiled values_proven document. The verdict asserts a conclusion; this hash is what the conclusion was computed from, and it is what makes REFUSED auditable rather than an opinion.

verdict.description: ELIGIBLE - every required value in the contract has a `proven` or human-`waived` row and the carriage rules hold. REFUSED - at least one does not; `refusals[]` says which. There is no third value: `mostly` is what a gate that cannot refuse produces.

refusals.description: Why, one row per unsatisfied clause. Required in substance on a REFUSED verdict - a refusal with no reason is not reviewable and cannot be argued with, which makes it indistinguishable from an outage.

clause.description: The contract clause or value id that refused (e.g. `V-est-2`, `carriage.require_entry_values_proven`).

admitted.description: What this station's own ADMIT verified on the way in: the upstream verdict it checked, and the values it therefore inherited rather than re-proved. Present on every station but the first. This is the field that makes the chain readable end to end from any single verdict.

prd_sha256.description: The work order this verdict closes. Optional only because the earliest stations predate a machine-rendered PRD; a station that minted one and does not cite it here has lost the ex-ante ordering.

fills_sha256.description: The append-only log the values were compiled from, at the moment of rendering. An append after this hash is a new log and needs a new verdict.
